title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet

epigraph.quote: Earnings are an opinion of the actuary; operating cash flow and unencumbered parent-company liquidity are facts.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.html: From FY2016 through FY2025, UnitedHealth Group compounded consolidated revenue at a 10.3% CAGR, rising from $184.8 billion to $447.6 billion [2, 4, 26, 27]. Annual operating cash flow expanded from $9.8 billion to a peak of $29.1 billion in 2023 before the 2024–2025 reset [2, 4, 26, 27]. A forensic review of the 10-year ledger shows both extraordinary cash-generation durability and the balance-sheet residue of a decade-long acquisition spree.

web_blocks.caption: UNH 10-Year P&L, Cash Flow & Balance Sheet Forensics ($ in Millions, except per-share & ratios)
web_blocks.takeaway: Net Income is attributable to UNH common shareholders [2, 26]. 9M 2026 balance-sheet figures (LT Debt $68,714M, Goodwill $112,974M) reflect the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q as of September 30, 2026 [29]. Across all 10 years, CFO exceeded Net Income every single year (1.29x–1.68x). Diluted share count also fell 6.4% from 968M in 2016 to 902M in Q3 2026 [7].

web_blocks.title: Balance Sheet Quality: Goodwill, Debt & Regulatory Capital

web_blocks.html: While cash conversion is elite, Q3 2026 Form 10-Q footnotes reveal heightened balance-sheet complexity beyond headline debt. First, Goodwill rose to $112.97 billion ($112,974 million) plus $20.38 billion in net intangibles—totaling $133.35 billion at September 30, 2026 [29]. That equals 42.6% of total assets ($312.78 billion) and 1.28x total equity ($104.13 billion), leaving tangible equity deeply negative; notably, $42.77 billion of YE2025 goodwill (38.7%) sits in Optum Health [2, 29]. The Q3 goodwill jump reflects a $3.0 billion acquisition closed July 2, 2026 ($1.5 billion cash plus a $1.5 billion deferred payable due within one year) [29].

Second, total debt stood at $74.33 billion at September 30, 2026 ($5,617 million short-term, including $2.9 billion of commercial paper at a 3.9% average rate, plus $68,714 million long-term). That debt fell $4.06 billion from $78.39 billion at year-end 2025 [29]. Debt-to-capital improved to 41.7% (targeting ~40.0%), backed by $21.0 billion in undrawn revolving credit facilities [2, 7, 29]. However, Moody's (A2), S&P Global (A+), and Fitch (A) all hold Negative outlooks on UNH's senior unsecured debt as of September 30, 2026 (A.M. Best A- Stable) [29]. Footnote forensics also uncover five balance-sheet items [2, 29]. First is a $2.2 billion uncommitted receivables financing facility ($5.9 billion sold in 9M 2026, $1.5 billion unremitted). Second is $(3,592) million in gross unrealized losses on available-for-sale debt securities, pushing AOCI to $(3,934) million. Third is $11.5 billion in loan receivables across Optum Financial and provider loans. Fourth is $4.8 billion in estimated put/call obligations on unconsolidated businesses plus $4.6 billion in operating lease liabilities (YE25 10-K Note 12). Fifth is deposit-accounting reinsurance reducing statutory capital requirements [2, 29].

web_blocks.title: Restricted Insurance Cash vs. Parent-Company Liquidity
paragraphs: At September 30, 2026, UNH held $25.8 billion in cash and cash equivalents within $78.3 billion of cash, AFS debt, and marketable equity securities ($86.6 billion total cash and investments) [29]. Yet only $1.2 billion sat available at the parent level for general corporate use [29]. Despite three Negative rating outlooks and limited unencumbered parent cash, UNH spent $5.03 billion on buybacks (13.8 million shares) and $6.17 billion on dividends in 9M 2026 [29]. In November 2026, the Board also authorized up to 50 million additional shares for repurchase (~5.6% of shares outstanding) alongside a $9.28 annualized dividend rate—making disciplined subsidiary dividend upstreaming essential [29, 37].

web_blocks.title: ROIC vs. Cost of Capital & Capital Allocation

web_blocks.html: On an unadjusted invested-capital basis (including $131B of goodwill and intangibles), UNH's 2025 ROIC compressed to ~7.5%–9.5% during the margin trough [1, 26]. That sat barely above an estimated 7.5%–8.0% WACC, down from 14%–16% ROIC in 2021–2023 [1, 26]. On a tangible invested-capital basis, however, returns remain very high because insurance float funds working capital. In 2026, 9M EBIT rebounded to $23.5 billion and full-year CFO is tracking ~$24–$25 billion [6, 7]. ROIC is now recovering cleanly above WACC, backing a 12.6% 5-year dividend growth rate ($8.73/sh paid in 2025) and $5.0 billion+ in 2026 buybacks [6, 7].

book_paragraphs: When you and I open a ten-year financial statement on a company, we look for two things: steady cash generation and hidden balance-sheet stress. UnitedHealth Group's ten-year ledger from 2016 through 2025 tells a story of two halves. The first eight years brought relentless, almost metronomic compounding. The last two years brought balance-sheet digestion and margin compression that are only now clearing in 2026.

Look first at the income statement and cash flow statement together. Revenue grew every single year for a decade, more than doubling from $184.8 billion in 2016 to $447.6 billion in 2025. Even more impressive is cash conversion. In every single year of the last ten—including 2024's cyberattack and 2025's 41% operating-income drop—operating cash flow exceeded net income by 29% to 68%. Over that decade, UNH generated roughly $191 billion in cumulative free cash flow while spending under 1% of revenue on capital expenditures. In the first nine months of 2026 alone, operating cash flow jumped 35% year-over-year to $25.1 billion.

Now look at the other side of the ledger, because that is where disciplined analysts earn their keep. To build Optum into a $270 billion powerhouse, UNH wrote huge acquisition checks. It bought Catamaran, Surgical Care Affiliates, DaVita Medical Group, Change Healthcare, LHC Group, and Amedisys. As a result, goodwill and net intangibles ballooned to $131 billion by the end of 2025, or 42% of total assets and 1.31 times shareholders' equity. Meanwhile, total debt more than doubled from $33 billion in 2016 to $78.4 billion in 2025, lifting annual interest expense to $4.0 billion.

There is a second balance-sheet nuance you should always remember when analyzing any major insurer: not all cash on the balance sheet belongs to the parent company to spend freely. At mid-year 2026, UNH held $28.6 billion in cash and $50.3 billion in debt securities. Yet only $1.1 billion of that cash sat unencumbered at the parent level for general corporate use. The rest sits inside regulated insurance subsidiaries to protect policyholders under state statutory capital rules. That is why lifting UnitedHealthcare's underwriting margin from 2.7% back toward 4%–5% matters so much. Healthy subsidiary profits enable upstream dividends to pay down debt, fund the $8 billion annual dividend, and buy back shares.

The encouraging news in 2026 is that management recognized the leverage limit. UNH paused blockbuster M&A, paid down $3.1 billion of debt in the first nine months of 2026, and cut its debt-to-capital ratio to 41.7% toward its 40% target. During the 2025 trough, return on invested capital—weighed down by $131 billion of goodwill—dipped uncomfortably close to the cost of capital. As operating earnings rebound in 2026, the spread between ROIC and WACC is widening once again.

Finally, look at the debt maturity wall and capital-return hierarchy so you can judge balance-sheet resilience for yourself. Per the 2025 Form 10-K, UNH faces manageable debt maturities of roughly $3.0 billion to $3.7 billion per year from 2026 through 2029. Nearly $60 billion of its long-term debt is laddered out beyond 2030 at fixed investment-grade coupons. Against projected 2026 operating cash flow of $24 billion to $25 billion and CapEx under $4 billion, the math is comfortable. UNH can easily pay its $4 billion interest bill, fund $8 billion in annual dividends, retire $3 billion in debt, and buy back $5 billion of shares—all without touching restricted subsidiary capital. For long-term investors, that laddered debt profile removes near-term refinancing risk while management completes the multi-year operational turnaround across UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health.

Reading the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q footnotes adds crucial nuance to UNH's deleveraging story. While gross debt fell to $74.3 billion (including $2.9 billion in commercial paper) and debt-to-capital improved to 41.7%, three of four major credit rating agencies—Moody's, S&P, and Fitch—carry Negative outlooks on UNH's senior unsecured debt. Goodwill climbed to $113.0 billion (and $133.4 billion with intangibles, or 42.6% of total assets) after a $3.0 billion July 2026 acquisition that left a $1.5 billion deferred payable due within one year. Off-balance-sheet and working-capital footnotes also show $5.9 billion in receivables sold during 9M 2026 under a $2.2 billion financing facility, $3.59 billion in gross unrealized losses on bond holdings, $11.5 billion in loan receivables, and $4.8 billion in unconsolidated put-call obligations. With only $1.2 billion of UNH's $25.8 billion cash unencumbered at the parent level—and a fresh November 2026 Board authorization to repurchase up to 50 million shares—capital allocation must balance shareholder returns tightly against rating-agency deleveraging expectations.

book_callouts.title: The Goodwill & Leverage Check
book_callouts.text: UNH's cash conversion is elite (CFO/Net Income >1.29x for 10 straight years), but its $110.5B goodwill and $74.3B total debt mean capital allocation must prioritize deleveraging and organic execution over large M&A.
bullets: Goodwill + Intangibles (Q3 2026): $133.4B (42.6% of total assets; $1.5B M&A payable due within 1 year).
Debt-to-Capital: 41.7% at Q3 2026 ($74.3B debt; Moody's/S&P/Fitch Negative outlooks; $1.2B parent cash).
